newsitem.title: USA: New Jersey police officer suspended after dispute.
newsitem.headline: New Jersey police officer suspended after dispute.

text.p: A suburban New Jersey police officer has been suspended after arresting and handcuffing an elderly woman who complained about where he parked his car, authorities said Tuesday.

Officer Wayne Seich arrested 71-year-old Elise Kitchen, a neighbourhood woman who has known him since he was six years old, after she complained that his patrol car was blocking a busy intersection in Edison, New Jersey, said her attorney Michael Cohan.
The angry police officer pushed her to the ground as he put her in handcuffs, said Cohan and Kitchen's husband Edward.
Seich charged the woman with assaulting a police officer. Her attorney said she raised her arms in self defence.
Police confirmed that her arms were bruised, and she was taken to a local hospital for an examination.
The officer has been suspended with pay pending an investigation, said Edison Deputy Police Chief Angelo Bekarian.

"If the investigation shows that Officer Seich violated our regulations, I can, and will, file charges against him," Bekarian said. He said he could not comment on any details of the allegations against the officer.
The incident occurred Saturday, when Kitchen said she was forced to drive around the officer's patrol car while he was parked and chatting with a friend.
She called police to complain, and the officer came to her home where the confrontation occurred, said her attorney.
